report.summary: The /wrk2-api/post/compose path is failing with HTTP 500 because compose-post-service cannot resolve the hostname user-service: its own logs repeat "TSocket::open() getaddrinfo() <Host: user-service Port: 9090> Name or service not known" from 00:54:34.186 through 00:54:43.891, and nginx-thrift logs the propagated error "ComposePost(): compost_post failure: Could not resolve host for client socket." with 500 responses. The DNS fault is visible in the cluster's DNS config: the CoreDNS Corefile in ConfigMap kube-system/coredns contains an injected `template ANY ANY user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local { match "^user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local\.$" rcode NXDOMAIN fallthrough }` stanza, so the exact FQDN of user-service is answered NXDOMAIN and getaddrinfo returns EAI_NONAME even though the Service (ClusterIP 10.96.30.40) and its Endpoint (10.244.7.255) exist. That ConfigMap is the one mounted as /etc/coredns/Corefile by the 2-replica coredns Deployment, and its last write is by kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-24T00:54:25Z. user-service itself is up and serving (pod Ready with 0 restarts, compose_creator_server spans of 7-8 microseconds, no error spans), so it is not the failing component; only compose-post-service's name lookup for it is broken. Observed impact is limited to compose, which in this sampled window is the only workload with an elevated error count (78 lines for compose-post-service and 78 for nginx-thrift versus 1-4 startup lines elsewhere). The investigation window only covers ~26 s of application runtime, so no pre/post latency or error baseline exists and the failure ratio cannot be measured.

All social-network pods, including compose-post-service, user-service and nginx-thrift, were newly created between 00:54:18Z and 00:54:23Z with restartCount 0 and Ready containers, and the coredns pods started 00:54:25Z, so the observable application window starts about 26 s before the authorized window end.

Mechanism: the template stanza answers NXDOMAIN for the only name that matches the kubernetes plugin's service record (user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local), and the search-domain fallbacks user-service.svc.cluster.local / user-service.cluster.local are also unresolvable, so getaddrinfo in compose-post-service ends with EAI_NONAME ("Name or service not known") and ComposePost aborts before calling user-service; nginx then turns that into HTTP 500.

The intermittent nature of the failure (getaddrinfo errors start at 00:54:34.186, yet compose traces at 00:54:34.087 and 00:54:35.926 still return HTTP 200 with compose_creator_server spans on user-service) is consistent with either already-established pooled connections (keepalive_ms 10000) bypassing new lookups or with only part of the 2-replica CoreDNS fleet serving the modified Corefile at that moment; the evidence here cannot distinguish these.

Rejected: user-service being down, unready or missing was not the cause; its pod is Ready with 0 restarts, its Service has ClusterIP 10.96.30.40 and a ready endpoint 10.244.7.255, and it successfully served compose_creator_server requests during the failure window.

Rejected: a crash loop or restart of compose-post-service or nginx-thrift is not the cause; both pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, no last-terminated state and no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff evidence, and the only recorded events for them are Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started.

Remove the `template ANY ANY user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local { ... rcode NXDOMAIN ... }` stanza from the Corefile in ConfigMap kube-system/coredns (revert to the standard Corefile) and let the reload plugin or a coredns rollout pick it up, then re-verify that compose-post-service resolves user-service and that /wrk2-api/post/compose stops returning 500.

Add a DNS-resolution smoke check (resolve every social-network Service FQDN from a client pod) and alerting on getaddrinfo/NXDOMAIN failures, since ordinary pod-readiness checks kept every service Ready while compose requests were failing.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
